title: Hotfix: reduce metrics cardinality from fallback routing labels
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Internal-only hotfix: reduces time series explosion on fallback-routing metrics by removing high-cardinality tags and introducing a bounded classification label. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context: During the Feb 14 incident response, multiple Console dashboards (Saturation Overview + Routing/Fallback drilldowns) slowed to a crawl and some alerts stopped evaluating on time. The root cause was a time series explosion on routing/fallback metrics after we started emitting per-request fallback detail labels in the serving/control-plane pipeline. Those labels included values that are effectively unbounded (e.g., fallback_target_model, fallback_reason_detail, source_pool_id, and an occasionally-unique route_override_id). On busy regions this pushed cardinality high enough to cause query latency spikes and ingestion pressure.

This PR is a hotfix to immediately bound metric cardinality without losing the ability to answer the question responders actually need: "Are we falling back? Where? And is it capacity-driven or policy-driven?".

Changes: 1) Remove unbounded labels from fallback metrics: dropped fallback_target_model, route_override_id, source_pool_id, and fallback_reason_detail from the primary counters and histograms. 2) Introduce a bounded fallback_class label (enum): {"none", "capacity", "policy", "compat", "error"} derived from existing routing decision fields. 3) Keep a single low-cardinality fallback_to_family label for coarse attribution (e.g., "llama", "mistral", "other"), only when fallback_class != "none". 4) Add guardrails in the metrics emitter: hard cap on allowed label keys for fallback metrics; if additional keys are attempted, they are ignored and a single internal counter routing_metrics_label_drop_total{metric="fallback"} is incremented. 5) Update dashboard queries to use fallback_class + region + service rather than fallback_target_model.

Why this is safe: This is limited to internal metrics emission and dashboard wiring; the routing behavior is unchanged. The only behavior change is which labels are exported. Existing alerts that depended on fallback_target_model will need to be updated (included in this PR for the standard pack). We validated the new time series counts in staging (peak QPS replay) and saw >95% reduction in series for fallback metrics.

Rollout/ops: - This should be deployed ASAP to production control-plane + metrics sidecars. - If responders need deep attribution (exact fallback target), they should use traces/logs for now; we still log full routing decisions with sampling and will follow up with a safe aggregated view.

Follow-ups (not in this hotfix): - Re-introduce richer attribution via logs-to-metrics aggregation (bounded) or exemplars. - Add automated cardinality budget tests in CI for metrics PRs touching routing tags. - Align incident-bot cards to use fallback_class instead of target-model labels.

Testing: - Unit tests for label allowlist + fallback_class mapping. - Local prom scrape sanity test. - Staging load replay (notes in comment).

Incident reference: internal thread "telemetry query latency spike during incident" and the hotfix request from SRE to unbreak dashboards/alerts quickly.
commits: metrics/routing: drop high-cardinality fallback labels and add fallback_class enum
metrics: add label allowlist + routing_metrics_label_drop_total counter
dashboards: update fallback panels to group by fallback_class + region
tests: add coverage for fallback_class mapping and label filtering
conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Can you confirm which labels were the major contributors? Also want to ensure we still have a way to correlate capacity-driven fallback vs policy-driven. Nadia Rahman (author): Biggest offenders were fallback_target_model + route_override_id; combined they were effectively unbounded due to per-tenant overrides and experimentation. Added fallback_class so on-call can still bucket by cause. Full detail remains in routing decision logs/traces.

Allison Grant (review): Please update the alert queries in observability-pack to stop grouping by fallback_target_model; otherwise we’ll silently page-break. Also add a comment in the metric definition about cardinality budget. Nadia Rahman: Updated standard alerts/dashboards in this PR and added a doc note + emitter allowlist.

Mina Haddad (review): Concern: fallback_to_family could still be high if we ever include fine-grained families. Is that list bounded somewhere? Nadia Rahman: Yes—implemented as a fixed mapping for current catalog families with default "other"; no dynamic model string. Unit test included.

Aisha Bello (review): Any risk that changing labels will break existing SLO burn dashboards? Nadia Rahman: SLO dashboards use request_success/latency series, not fallback series. Only routing/fallback dashboards were impacted; updated here.

CI: first run failed due to jsonnet formatting (dashboards). Re-ran after fixing. Final checks green.

Approval: 4 approvals. Merged via squash. Deployment note added for on-call to prioritize shipping to prod today.
